pull.title: BIP-352: add test vectors for malleated p2pkh pubkey extraction
pull.body:
This adds two test vectors, each with a p2pkh input whose scriptSig also pushes another valid pubkey.

The first uses the scriptSig from the test in bitcoin/bitcoin#36338 by @theStack: `<sig> <pubkey> <bogus_sig> OP_OVER OP_CHECKSIG OP_IF <other_pubkey> OP_ENDIF`. Evaluating this scriptSig with a checker that accepts any signature leaves `<other_pubkey>` on top of the stack. The existing malleated p2pkh vector does not cover this.

The second is the `<dummy> OP_DROP <sig> <pubkey>` case @jonatack suggested in that PR, with a valid pubkey as the dummy. It catches an extractor that takes the first 33-byte push without checking its hash.

The expected values come from reference.py. btclib-wallet's vector tests also pass on the new file.

I ran Bitcoin Core's `bip352_tests` with the new file in place of its vendored copy:
- at the head of #36338 (cdfaa534), all 30 vectors pass;
- on master's code, the first new vector fails;
- on #36338 without its Hash160 check, the second new vector fails.

Core's test does not compare `input_pub_keys`, so each failure shows on the receiving side: the wrong key gives a wrong tweak, and no output is found.

*Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

events.body: With bitcoin/bitcoin#36338 merged, Core's master (db0bde16) passes all 30 vectors in this file, so Core and reference.py now agree on them.

events.body: @theStack @jonatack, a review of these two vectors would be welcome when you have time.

Tested e8603368 on macos<arm64>, ''Python 3.11.7'' . Steps: 1. Fetched pull/2323/head and copied bip-0352/send_and_receive_test_vectors.json into the Code Orange silent-payments lab (an educational Python BIP352 implementation: my own send/receive code, lab-provided input-key extraction). 2. Ran its send and receive graders. Result: 31/31 passing on both, including the two new vectors. Observation: the lab extracts the P2PKH key by checking every 33-byte window of the scriptSig against the scriptPubKey's hash160. A naive first-33-byte extractor returns the decoy key (02c6047f...) on "another pubkey pushed first", and the correct key on "failing OP_CHECKSIG". So the first vector doesn't catch naive extractors. Per the PR description, it targets evaluators with a permissive checker, which I didn't test.

ACK e8603368af23ae185eb81500923fa23421d650c8

Ran `reference.py` against the updated vectors and checked both new `scriptSig` encodings, `Hash160` matches, tweaks, and BIP-340 signatures. The changelog entry and version bump to 1.1.3 look good too.
